items.headline: RBI's rate panel begins three-day meeting; 8 of 10 economists expect a hike to 5.50%
items.summary: The MPC meets October 5–7 with the decision due on the 7th. Most economists polled expect a 25-basis-point hike from 5.25%, the first since February 2023. Ongoing: hike expectations have built all week.
items.rationale: A hike lifts loan rates and G-Sec yields, hitting housing, vehicles and consumer credit, while supporting the rupee and lenders' margins at first. Markets have largely priced it; guidance on further hikes matters most.

economies.why: Wider rate gap supports the rupee

items.headline: Foreign investors have pulled over ₹3 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026; selling continues into October
items.summary: FPI outflows passed ₹3 lakh crore in nine months and continued in October. The Nifty fell 3.1% last week to 22,421.95, an eighth straight weekly loss and the longest losing run in 25 years. Escalating.
items.rationale: Persistent foreign selling hits index heavyweights such as large lenders and oil and gas names, pressures the rupee and keeps valuations under strain until global yields ease.

industries.why: Oil and gas among worst hit

items.headline: Rupee seen trading 95.30–96.80 per dollar in October as record reserves offset outflows
items.summary: A report sees the rupee broadly sideways in October. Forex reserves at a record $785.71 billion and trade deals support it; global yields and FPI outflows of about $5.9 billion in September weigh. Ongoing pressure near 96.
items.rationale: A rupee near record lows lifts IT and pharma exporters' earnings but raises the cost of oil and other imports; ample reserves let the RBI cap volatility.

economies.why: Pressure near record lows, capped by reserves

items.headline: OPEC+ holds November output steady; Brent near $101 as supply stays ~5 million bpd below pre-war
items.summary: OPEC+ kept its 31.1 million bpd target for November, extending October's pause. Core members pumped 25 million bpd in August, about 5 million below February. Brent eased 0.9% to $101.31. Ongoing: crude above $100 all week.
items.rationale: No extra supply keeps crude near $100, India's biggest macro headwind: a wider import bill, rupee pressure, fuel inflation and squeezed margins for marketers, airlines and crude-linked manufacturers.

items.headline: India's crude imports hit a 2026 high of 5.26 million bpd as Gulf supply recovers via ship-to-ship transfers
items.summary: September imports reached 5.26 million bpd; Gulf producers supplied 39% and Iraq became the second-largest supplier. Middle East shipments are near 98% of pre-conflict levels. Easing supply risk despite Hormuz attacks.
items.rationale: Secure crude volumes reduce the risk of fuel shortages and emergency buying, supporting refiners' runs, though prices near $100 keep the import bill high.

items.headline: Iran says Hormuz won't reopen until its conditions are met; tanker struck, five Indian crew rescued
items.summary: Iran said the strait stays closed until its conditions are met. A Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck near Oman, with five Indian seafarers rescued, and explosions were reported near a ship off Yemen. Ongoing for a fifth day.
items.rationale: Attacks keep war-risk insurance, freight and crude risk premiums high on India's main oil and LNG routes, and put Indian crews at risk.

industries.why: Freight and insurance costs stay high

items.headline: Ukraine vows more strikes on Russian refineries, threatening global diesel supply
items.summary: Zelenskyy said Ukraine will step up attacks on Russian refineries after Moscow's new airstrike campaign; Ukraine estimates over 45% of Russia's refining capacity has been knocked out. New escalation.
items.rationale: Less Russian refining tightens global diesel supply: export-oriented Indian refiners can earn wider diesel margins, but higher product prices add to fuel inflation.

items.headline: India–US trade talks still snag on Russian oil as new US law allows tariffs of up to 100%
items.summary: February's interim deal cut US tariffs on Indian goods to 18% in return for halting Russian oil purchases. A US law passed in September authorises tariffs of up to 100% on big buyers of Russian energy. Ongoing risk.
items.rationale: Any lapse on Russian oil risks steep US tariffs on Indian exports, while giving up discounted crude raises the import bill; the uncertainty weighs on exporters and foreign investors.

industries.why: Discounted Russian crude off the table

items.headline: Indian IT majors head into results week expecting their weakest September quarter in three years
items.summary: Large IT services firms are expected to report muted revenue growth with stable margins as clients keep discretionary budgets tight. A global IT bellwether raised its FY27 outlook to 3–6% growth but saw no change in demand. Earnings season starts this week.
items.rationale: Weak growth at index-heavy IT firms limits earnings support for Indian equities, though AI projects and a weak rupee cushion margins.

industries.why: Weakest September quarter in three years
